soundness_flags.label: def:population-decoder and thm:exact-ratio-decoder
soundness_flags.one_line: The parent-pruning predicate U_i ⟂ U_{B_i\setminus A} | U_A names no probability law; it must explicitly be conditional independence under P^0 (after defining all U coordinates), otherwise the minimization and claimed faithful pruning are undefined.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:simultaneous-confidence-edges
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The confidence statement assumes, rather than constructs, a simultaneous evaluation-law L1 ratio-error event and uses a fixed, non-data-driven radius.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Familywise ancestral-edge validity conditional on the stated first-stage event, with unconditional probability obtained by adding its failure probability.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: oeq:generated-rank-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The uniform C1 log-ratio contract and the optional asymptotically linear first-stage representation are inputs, not results of this proposal.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The requested coordinate-rate and expansion are conditional on the stated uniform first-stage contract; construction and attainability of that contract remain open.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 5–6, Theorems 3.2 and 3.4; p. 9, “Identifiability From One Intervention per Node for Any n”
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3.2 is the bivariate one-perfect-intervention-per-node result under condition (3.2); Theorem 3.4 uses paired single-node perfect interventions for arbitrary n; the paper explicitly conjectures the one-intervention arbitrary-n extension and identifies target misalignment as combinatorial.

With one perfect stochastic intervention per node, CauCA obtains componentwise identification up to scaling in a model indexed by a known DAG G; the surrounding text explicitly describes the known-graph setting.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 6, Theorem 3.4; pp. 2 and 6, measurement-model and isolated-edge discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3.4 identifies a maximal measurement model from a complete intervention family up to isolated latent edges under its graphical assumptions, including the no-imaginary-subset case.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 23–24, Assumption D.1 and Corollary D.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Corollary D.1 gives elementwise-diffeomorphism identification from one imperfect intervention per node under a topologically ordered target assumption; the paper calls order recovery an orthogonal subproblem requiring additional assumptions.
The paper develops MMD two-sample tests and distribution-free/asymptotic concentration-calibration results for observed samples, not learned likelihood-ratio inputs shared across graph edges.

The article derives stochastic expansions, rates, and asymptotic distributions for nonparametric regression with estimated covariates; it does not address generated indicator thresholds in a conditional-CDF process.

source_verification_receipts.version: Statistics & Probability Letters 201 (2023); theorem-level journal text inaccessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The source establishes that the work concerns uniform bias, rate, and asymptotic-linear results for local-linear conditional-distribution estimation; exact theorem numbering/formula comparison remains source-verification work.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define all parent-pruning conditional independences under P^0, state that the minimization is over subsets of B_i under that law, and add the resulting faithfulness/pruning implication explicitly to Theorem 2.

Add a standalone observable-order lemma stating both no-false-positive ancestry edges and inclusion of every ancestral cover, then use it to justify that every admissible topological order contains all parents before conditional-rank recovery.

Make the statistical component materially stronger by specifying a feasible ratio learner and proving its uniform C1 contract on the bounded subclass, or retain it as a clearly separate conditional OEQ rather than presenting the contract as implementation-ready.

State precisely the comparator regime against von Kugelgen et al.—including which smoothness/support assumptions are narrowed while intervention count is reduced—and add a boundary corollary showing the n=2 specialization is exactly the published witness setting.

recommended_next_step: Revise the decoder to make its parent-pruning law explicit, then advance the population genericity/one-intervention identification kernel to Stage 0 while retaining the two first-stage assumptions as accepted conditional scope.
